narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Split from #4798. Production `task release` Step 5 arms `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` (20 minutes) only on the suite gate (`ts:check-lane` / `verify:consumer-test-lane`). A hung non-suite gate, including `verify:ac` first, can run past that wall with no `[5/13]` PASS/FAIL/124. Do not raise `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`.

#4798 keeps the cycle refuse (check-integrated `verify:ac` must not re-enter `task check`) and leftover-complete must-move. This issue is the hang bound only.

## Observed (from #4798 panel at 5d45d1557b181383a79c6705e68fc3daeb34d74a)

- `runReleaseCheck` sets `timeoutMs` on in-process check seams; `cached-orchestrator.ts` forwards it only inside `isSuiteCheckGate`.
- Non-suite `captureSpawn` is `spawnSync` with no timeout and no `killDescendantTree`. On Windows a `spawnSync` timeout would kill `task.exe` and orphan node/vitest descendants.
- `releaseCheckEnv` exports `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT=1` and `CHECK_MODE=full` with no deadline. Nested `task check` constructs fresh seams with `timeoutMs` undefined.
- v0.119.4 last printed line was `check: product AC gate verify:ac first (#3284)` at ~1492s with no 124. v0.119.3 / #4744 reached the suite and 124'd; that suite-duration wall is not this issue (#4744 is closed ingest-ready while CHANGELOG still says the 20-minute wall is leftover).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A hung non-suite gate under `runReleaseCheck` (including `verify:ac`) exits 124 inside 20 minutes via process-tree kill (`runSupervisedGate` / `killDescendantTree`), not `spawnSync` timeout.
- [ ] Nested `task check` / child processes inherit a remaining-time deadline or are refused under `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT`.
- [ ] Exit 124 copy names the actual gate, not "vitest coverage hang", when AC or another non-suite gate was the site.
- [ ] Do not raise `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`.

## Out of scope

- Cycle refuse of `swarm.verify_commands: ["task check"]` inside check-integrated `verify:ac` (stays on #4798).
- Cheapening `ts:check-lane` to finish under 20 minutes (closed #4744 wall).

Refs #4798, #4744, #4591, #2652.

## Verdict

The refutation target survives: at `ac500e1a019a620625d4717b32b84c92b2c5335b`, `runReleaseCheck` supplies `timeoutMs`, but `dispatchCachedTaskCheck` forwards it only through the suite-only branch; non-suite gates still use unsupervised `spawnSync`. The existing `runSupervisedGate` / `killDescendantTree` path is the right primitive. The proposed contract is not yet safe to bind because it does not close the whole-Step-5 deadline or nested-entry identity precisely enough.

## F1 — One relative timeout per gate is not the Step 5 wall

classification: blocks-the-design

Evidence: `packages/core/src/release/preflight.ts:75-87` passes one relative `timeoutMs`; `packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts:309-386` loops over gates and gives the full value only to the suite supervisor. The acceptance text asks for a "remaining-time deadline" only in the nested-child bullet, while the first bullet can be satisfied by arming a fresh 20-minute timer when each gate starts.

Concrete failure mode: several successful non-suite gates consume substantial time, then `verify:ac` (or a later non-suite gate) receives a fresh 20 minutes. Step 5 still runs beyond 20 minutes even though the new isolated gate-timeout test passes. A zero/negative remainder handled only by `setTimeout(0)` can also spawn work after the budget is already exhausted.

Disposition consequence: the lean cannot bind as written. Define one deadline at `runReleaseCheck` entry, require every uncached gate to receive `max(0, deadline-now)`, and refuse before spawn when no budget remains. Tests need an injected clock and at least: elapsed-before-first-gate, elapsed-between-gates, and expired-before-spawn cases. The invariant should be the Step 5 wall, not N independent 20-minute gate walls.

## F2 — `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT` is not a nesting discriminator

classification: blocks-the-design

Evidence: `releaseCheckEnv` sets `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT=1` before the legitimate first-level dispatch (`preflight.ts:26-44, 75-87`). The uncached orchestrator path then legitimately shells the aggregate `task check` with that same environment (`check/orchestrator.ts:43-78`). No deadline or recursion-depth environment mechanism exists at this SHA.

Concrete failure mode: implementing the acceptance alternative as "refuse `task check` whenever `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT=1`" either rejects the valid first-level uncached entry or, if exempted ad hoc, leaves recursive entries indistinguishable. Conversely, propagating only another relative duration lets each nested process mint a fresh wall.

Disposition consequence: require a distinct owned field for nesting/deadline identity, not the preflight boolean. Prefer an inherited absolute release deadline plus an entry/depth marker; validate malformed or expired values fail-closed. If recursion refusal remains an allowed strategy, state exactly which boundary increments depth and prove first-level dispatch still works.

## F3 — Generalize supervision without turning all gates into suite state

classification: sharpens-framing

Evidence: `runSupervisedGate` is already a generic command/args/process-tree supervisor in behavior, but its storage and callers are suite-shaped: `.deft-scratch/check-suite`, `lastSuiteTeeRel`, `lastSuiteTeeText`, `suiteActuallyRan`, and suite-specific worker diagnostics. `formatNamedCauseFailure` already accepts `hangTimeout`, yet `cached-orchestrator.ts:492-501` does not pass `SupervisedGateResult.timedOut`; `runReleaseCheck` then collapses every 124 to "vitest coverage hang" (`preflight.ts:88-92`).

Concrete failure mode: a mechanical widening of the existing suite branch can let a successful non-suite gate overwrite suite evidence or apply suite cleanup/diagnostics to the wrong gate. A timed-out AC gate can still receive the suite-specific remedy unless `timedOut` and `gateId` stay coupled through named-cause formatting and the Step 5 result.

Disposition consequence: keep one generic process-tree supervision core, but keep suite tee/stamp state conditional on `isSuiteCheckGate`. Carry `{ gateId, timedOut }` through completion and named-cause output; make the outer release message report the actual timed-out gate rather than replace it with a suite-only string.

## F4 — Injection / swarm lens

classification: footnote

Evidence: the change touches shared environment and descendant-process concurrency, so the lens fires. Existing containment is sound in shape: Windows uses `taskkill /T /F /PID`, POSIX uses a detached process group when a timeout is armed, and the supervisor passes fixed command/argv assembled by the orchestrator. The new inherited deadline/depth values are control-plane shared state.

Concrete failure mode: accepting arbitrary inherited strings or logging the environment wholesale would let ambient state extend/disable the bound or leak unrelated values. The current named-cause path already filters env-shaped output.

Disposition consequence: no additional blocker beyond F1/F2; parse a closed numeric format, cap it at the release-owned deadline, scrub it outside release preflight, and never echo the ambient environment.

## Mechanism inventory and verification

- Re-ran 75 focused tests across `release/preflight`, `check/orchestrator`, `suite-gate-supervisor`, and `named-cause`; all passed. Those tests confirm the present suite-only behavior and tree-kill primitive, but none proves a whole-Step-5 deadline across multiple gates or distinguishes nested entry.
- Existing reusable mechanisms: `runSupervisedGate`, `superviseChild`, `killDescendantTree`, `SupervisedGateResult.timedOut`, per-gate `gateId`, `formatNamedCauseFailure({ hangTimeout })`, and `releaseCheckEnv`.

Road not taken: wrap the entire aggregate `task check` once and kill its tree at the release deadline. That gives the cleanest wall, but the parent then lacks reliable actual-gate identity for the required 124 copy. I would switch to that design if the check process exposed a durable current-gate progress channel; without it, per-gate supervision under one inherited deadline preserves both the wall and the gate name.

Steelman: a fresh 20-minute timer per gate is simpler and directly fixes the observed `verify:ac` hang. It would flip my F1 verdict only if the intended invariant were explicitly "20 minutes after each gate starts" rather than the release Step 5 wall; the issue title, the existing release constant, and the remaining-time language point to the latter.

Refutation of Stop 1 field refutation-target (comment 5746391787). Pin SHA ac500e1a019a620625d4717b32b84c92b2c5335b. Re-verified by reading those files, not by restating the write-back cites.

Diagnosis half holds. Remedy half does not bind as written.

Measured: runReleaseCheck sets checkSeams.timeoutMs to RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS (packages/core/src/release/preflight.ts 75-77). dispatchTaskCheck takes the cached path by default (packages/core/src/check/orchestrator.ts 50-54). cached-orchestrator forwards timeoutMs only inside isSuiteCheckGate (372-386). Non-suite captureSpawn is spawnSync with no timeout and no killDescendantTree (82-93). releaseCheckEnv sets DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT and CHECK_MODE=full and has no deadline field (27-44). Uncached orchestrator.ts does pass timeout to spawnSync (72-114); docs/RELEASING.md says release does not take that path.

## 1. Inherited-deadline conjunct has no carrier and drops 124

blocks-the-design

Evidence: Nested acceptance commands run through defaultLiteralAcceptanceRunner, which is spawnSync({ shell: true }) with no timeout (packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/run.ts 33-44). Nested task check is a new process. It does not receive CheckOrchestratorSeams.timeoutMs. There is no remaining-time env today. If that nested check is given a deadline by some later env and returns 124, verify:ac treats it as a command failure (expected 0, got 124) and runReleaseCheck takes "task check failed (exit 1)" (preflight.ts 107), not the code === 124 branch (88-92).

Failure mode: Binding runSupervisedGate plus an inherited deadline as one MUST either no-ops the deadline half (seams do not cross the AC spawnSync boundary) or, if the deadline is implemented only on nested check, Step 5 never 124s on the observed hang (AC-first line, nested check). The v0.119.4 symptom is the AC gate child running unbounded, not a missing env on a child that already 124s.

Disposition: Outer tree-kill of the non-suite gate child is the 124 bound for P1. Inherited remaining-time is a new env contract plus 124 propagation through the literal-acceptance runner, or the #4798 refuse under DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT. Those are not this issue hang primitive. Do not bind the compound as one remedy. Cycle refuse stays on #4798; this arc must 124 even when nested task check still happens.

## 2. Name the hang-kill primitive, not the suite wrapper

sharpens-framing

Evidence: runSupervisedGate is the sync worker wrapper that always pruneSuiteTees, always tees into .deft/check-tees, and is documented "Hygiene gates keep captureSpawn" (packages/core/src/check/suite-gate-supervisor.ts 1-6, 63-68; superviseChild 275-309). cached-orchestrator assigns lastSuiteTeeRel / lastSuiteTeeText only in that suite branch (390-399), and suiteActuallyRan reads that tee. Tests lock a single suite plan and timeout-only-when-set (packages/core/src/check/orchestrator.test.ts 318-364). killDescendantTree already exists (packages/core/src/check/suite-gate-supervisor-lib.ts 160-181). consumer-test-lane defaultSpawn already does async spawn plus killDescendantTree plus 124 without suite tees (packages/core/src/consumer-test-lane/evaluate.ts 125-171), with its own 15-minute default, not RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS.

Failure mode: Binding runSupervisedGate as the non-suite remedy either feeds AC output into suite-tee identity or starts a Worker+tee for every hygiene gate under release (FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES has AC plus many fast gates before ts:check-lane). Hang P1 can still 124 on a naive reuse because fail-fast returns before suiteActuallyRan; the coupling is still a false suite-tee contract and a release-only behavior change the lean does not name.

Disposition: Recut the remedy to a tee-optional sync supervisor (same Worker/Atomics.wait need because the orchestrator is sync) that calls killDescendantTree at timeoutMs. Keep suite tees on isSuiteCheckGate. Do not invent a second hang constant. Do not raise RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS.

Road-not-taken: wrap the entire in-process dispatch as one supervised child from runReleaseCheck. That gives one Step 5 wall and kills nested trees, but drops onCheckComplete / suiteActuallyRan unless IPC is added, and cannot name the hung gate without a side channel. Rejected because acceptance wants the actual gate on the 124 copy. Flip if the operator prefers one envelope over per-gate names.

Steelman: smallest diff is pass timeoutMs into the existing runSupervisedGate for every gate when set. That would 124 hung AC. Flip this heading if superviseChild tees become optional and lastSuiteTee stays suite-only; then naming runSupervisedGate is the sync path, not the suite product.

## 3. 124 copy and hang named-cause are still suite-shaped

sharpens-framing

Evidence: Any 124 from runReleaseCheck prints vitest coverage hang (preflight.ts 88-91). packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts Step 5 auto-hatch text says cancel hung vitest (line 417). extractHangDetectorCause names hang only when hangTimeout is true, the gate is in SUITE_HANG_DETECTOR_GATES (ts:check-lane, verify:consumer-test-lane), or a ts:check-lane last-file tick exists (packages/core/src/check/named-cause.ts 61-65, 205-221). cached-orchestrator formatNamedCauseFailure does not pass hangTimeout (492-501). A verify:ac 124 therefore misses the hang-cause path unless that flag is plumbed. remedyForGate on a hang-cause still says cheapen Windows vitest coverage.

Failure mode: Hang bound lands, operator and recovery copy still diagnose vitest. classifyStep5Failure already treats exit 124 as REAL_FAILURE (packages/core/src/release/auto-hatch.ts 89), so this is misdiagnosis, not a skip-ci hatch. Still violates the acceptance line that 124 copy names the actual gate.

Disposition: Pass timedOut/hangTimeout from the supervisor; name the gate id in the preflight 124 string; stop using SUITE_HANG_DETECTOR_GATES as the only hang identity. Do not treat last-file as required for a non-suite hang.

## 4. Injection / swarm lens (process tree, tees, nested identity)

sharpens-framing

This target changes concurrency and shared state: Worker threads, process-tree kill, .deft/check-tees, sessionId in tee names, nested go-task -> node -> cmd.exe /c -> task.exe under spawnSync(shell: true) on Windows.

killDescendantTree is taskkill /T /F on a PID (win32) or kill(-pid) when detached (POSIX; superviseChild detaches only off win32 when timeoutMs is set). PID-scoped, not swarm-wide. Ambient task check does not arm timeoutMs, so dest workers are not this kill. Risk that remains: Windows tree walk from the outer task.exe PID can miss breakaway grandchildren from shell:true spawnSync; that is the same orphan class the issue already names for spawnSync timeout. A Job Object assigned at the supervised spawn is the stronger control; tree kill after the fact is the existing one. Reusing suite tees for every release hygiene gate shares pruneSuiteTees across identities that suiteActuallyRan treats as suite evidence.

Do not close a safety case on reviewer attention. Deterministic control is Job Object or proven tree-kill from the supervised child PID, plus tests that a hung shell:true grandchild is gone after 124.

## 5. Uncached spawnSync timeout is not the fix

footnote

Inventory: uncached dispatchTaskCheck already 124s via spawnSync timeout (orchestrator.ts 92-97, 111-113). Release cached path is the production Step 5 path. Switching release to noCache would re-introduce the Windows orphan the issue already recorded. consumer-test-lane 15-minute inner wall is a second hang layer on a suite gate, not a non-suite bound. --allow-skip-ci remains incident-only. Leave those in place; extend hang-kill to non-suite children on the cached path.

## Verdict

Do not refute: RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS is armed only on the suite gate on the cached release path, so a hung non-suite gate including verify:ac never 124s, and the constant must not be raised.

Refute: the remedy is runSupervisedGate / killDescendantTree plus an inherited deadline. Bind outer tree-kill of non-suite gate children (tee-optional sync supervisor) and recut 124 copy/named-cause off the suite identity. Treat remaining-time inheritance and DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT refuse as separate contracts, the latter already on #4798.

Round 1 critic, refutation charter, seat claude. Pin-read every anchor at `ac500e1a019a620625d4717b32b84c92b2c5335b` with `git show`. Target under refutation is the Stop 1 `refutation-target:` field: *"RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS is armed only on the suite gate, so a hung non-suite gate including verify:ac never 124, and the remedy is runSupervisedGate / killDescendantTree plus an inherited deadline, not raising the constant."*

Verdict up front: the **conclusion** survives and the **premise does not**. The constant is armed in two places, not one, and the second one is a whole-run wall carrying the exact Windows-orphan defect this issue raises. The named remedy, applied as written, also converts a 20-minute Step-5 wall into a ~49x20-minute one without touching the constant.

## Anchors re-verified (not restated from the gate stamp)

Confirmed by running the reads, not by trusting the cites:

- `packages/core/src/release/constants.ts:42-44` -- `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 20 * 60 * 1000`. Holds.
- `packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts:386` -- `timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs` appears exactly once, inside the `isSuiteCheckGate(gateSpec) && ...` branch at 372-373. The non-suite arm at 407-416 is `captureSpawn`, which is `spawnSync` with `encoding: "utf8"` and no `timeout` key. Holds.
- `packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts:66-74` -- `SUITE_CHECK_GATE_IDS` is exactly `["ts:check-lane", "verify:consumer-test-lane"]`, so `verify:ac` is non-suite. Holds.
- `packages/core/src/release/preflight.ts:77` -- `timeoutMs: seams.checkSeams?.timeoutMs ?? RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`, and `releaseCheckEnv` sets `RELEASE_PREFLIGHT_ENV` / `ENV_CHECK_MODE=full` with no deadline field. Holds.
- `suite-gate-supervisor-lib.ts:301-308` -- timer armed only when `plan.timeoutMs !== undefined`; `killDescendantTree` at the wall. Holds.

Two I checked that do **not** support findings, recorded so the panel does not re-spend them:

- Cache poisoning of a 124. `runWithCache` (`packages/core/src/cache/task-cache/executor.ts:43`) stores only `live.exitCode === 0`. A timed-out gate is never cached. No finding.
- Advisory swallow of a 124. `cached-orchestrator.ts:467` continues past a failing hygiene gate when `modeResolution.hygieneAdvisory`, but `resolveProductFirstCheckMode` (`product-first-done-gate/check-mode.ts:94`) returns `hygieneAdvisory: parsed !== "full"`, and `releaseCheckEnv` pins `full` and deletes `ENV_CHECK_AC_ONLY` / `ENV_HYGIENE_ADVISORY`. Off on Step 5 today. No finding, though it is an env-derived invariant no test on this path asserts.

## 1. blocks-the-design -- the constant is armed twice, and the second site is the one with the bug

**Evidence.** `packages/core/src/check/orchestrator.ts:72-97`. `dispatchTaskCheck` branches on `const useTaskCache = seams.useTaskCache !== false && !seams.noCache;`. Only the true arm reaches `dispatchCachedTaskCheck`. The false arm spawns the aggregate target through `defaultSpawn`, which at 105-115 passes `timeout: opts.timeoutMs` and `killSignal: "SIGTERM"` straight to `spawnSync`, and at 92-96 maps `result.signal === "SIGTERM" && result.status === null` to exit 124 with `check: timed out after 20m (Step 5 vitest coverage budget; #2652)`.

So `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` is armed on **every** gate on that path -- as one whole-run wall, covering `verify:ac` -- and the recorded premise "armed only on the suite gate" is false as a statement about the tree. The defensible statement is narrower: *armed only on the suite gate on the cached path, which is the production default because `runReleaseCheck` sets neither `useTaskCache: false` nor `noCache`.*

**Failure mode.** Two, and the second matters more.

(a) An implementer reading the recorded premise searches for one arming site, patches `cached-orchestrator.ts:386`, and ships. A release run with `--no-cache`, or any seam path setting `useTaskCache: false`, still takes the uncached arm -- where the 20-minute wall fires by `spawnSync` timeout against `task.exe` with `killSignal: "SIGTERM"`. On Windows that is precisely the orphaned-node/vitest-descendant shape AC1 exists to forbid, and this issue's acceptance as written never touches it. The issue closes with the orphan bug still reachable on a documented flag.

(b) The uncached arm is the inventory item that reframes the remedy, and the gate stamp's inventory line (suite supervisor, named-cause 124, spawn-heavy, allow-skip-ci) omits it. ## 4. sharpens-framing -- AC1 names a mechanism where it needs an observable, and the mechanism does not verify itself

**Evidence.** AC1 requires exit 124 inside 20 minutes **via process-tree kill (`runSupervisedGate` / `killDescendantTree`), not `spawnSync` timeout**. The stated reason for preferring that mechanism is orphan avoidance. But `killDescendantTree` (`suite-gate-supervisor-lib.ts:160-181`) on Windows dispatches `["/T", "/F", "/PID", String(pid)]` through `spawnSync("taskkill", ..., { windowsHide: true, stdio: "ignore" })` -- `stdio: "ignore"`, no return value inspected, no status check. `taskkill /T` walks the parent-child chain as it exists at kill time; a descendant that has already re-parented, or one spawned between the timer firing and `taskkill` running, is not in that tree. `superviseChild:311-320` then resolves on the **direct** child's exit event and returns 124 regardless.

**Failure mode.** The wall fires, `taskkill` partially succeeds, `superviseChild` reports 124, Step 5 correctly fails -- and orphaned vitest workers keep holding the coverage output and the tee handle. The next release run inherits a machine with stale node processes. Every clause of AC1 is satisfied and the pain that motivated preferring tree-kill over `spawnSync` timeout is not relieved. The criterion is written so that the mechanism **is** the acceptance, which means conformance can be demonstrated without the outcome.

**Disposition consequence.** Restate AC1's second half as the observable: no node/vitest descendant of the timed-out gate survives the 124, with a deterministic control -- enumerate descendants before the kill, re-enumerate after, assert empty, and escalate (a Windows Job Object with kill-on-close, or a second `taskkill` pass) when it is not. ## 5. sharpens-framing -- `runSupervisedGate` is built for one long child, and the remedy hands it 49 short ones

**Evidence.** Per invocation, `runSupervisedGate` (`suite-gate-supervisor.ts:63-131`) does a full `pruneSuiteTees` filesystem walk of the tee directory, `mintSuiteRunId`, `resolveWorkerPath` with an `existsSync`, a `new Worker(...)` thread spawn, a `SharedArrayBuffer` plus `MessageChannel`, an `Atomics.wait` block, and `worker.terminate()`. `superviseChild:279-282` then does `containedOpenExclusive` on a per-run tee file. `cached-orchestrator.ts:181` already calls `pruneSuiteTees` once at check entry, so the supervisor's own call is a second walk -- today 1-2 extra walks per run, at 49 gates it is 49, on the ambient `task check` dev loop and not only on release Step 5.

Today two gates are exposed; routing all 49 makes a missing compiled worker abort every check on gate 1. Separately, `containedOpenExclusive` is exclusive-create, so concurrent `task check` runs in one worktree contend on 49 creates and 49 prune walks over a single shared directory instead of 1-2.

**Failure mode.** A dev-loop `task check` regresses by 48 worker-thread spawns and 48 directory walks it did not previously pay; and a src-tree run without a compiled worker turns from "the suite gate throws" into "check aborts on the first gate with a stack trace."

## Injection / swarm lens (triggered: concurrency, process trees, shared state)

Firing because the target changes process-tree kill authority and writes to a directory shared across concurrent sessions. Not an N/A recital.

Already defended, and I am not raising these: gate argv is a source constant (`FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES`) composed by `checkGateSpawnArgs` / `checkGateCliArgv`, with no thread-derived or issue-derived input, so widening supervision adds no injection surface. Tee paths run through `sanitizeSessionDirName` and then `assertTeePathContained` against `projectRoot`, so per-gate use adds no path authority.

Not defended, and worth an acceptance line. `killDescendantTree` resolves a PID once inside the `setTimeout` callback and hands the bare number to `taskkill` in a separate process; between those, the child may exit and Windows may reuse the PID. Today that window opens at most twice per release run and only at the 20-minute mark. Arm 49 gates and it opens 49 times -- and under the deadline design of finding 2, late gates get **short** remaining windows, so timers fire near process exit far more often than at a 20-minute idle wall. ## Road not taken

Three mechanisms were live, and I did fork here rather than recite one.

(a) Forward `options.timeoutMs` to every gate through the existing `runSupervisedGate`. Rejected on findings 2 and 5: a duration is not a deadline, and the supervisor's per-call machinery is sized for one child.

(b) Restore the uncached arm's whole-run wall as a Step-5 backstop and fix only its kill. Attractive -- it already has the scope right and it is small -- but it bounds Step 5 without ever naming the gate, so AC3 stays unmet and the operator learns only that something hung.

(c) One absolute `deadlineAtMs` minted at `runReleaseCheck` entry, threaded through the seams, each gate armed at the remaining span, supervisor stays suite-only, non-suite gates get a small verified tree-kill seam. This is what I recommend: it is the only one that satisfies AC1, AC2, and AC3 together, and it makes the child-inheritance half of AC2 fall out rather than needing separate design.

## Steelman of the strongest rejected position

The strongest case against me is for (a), and it is not weak. One audited mechanism beats two: `runSupervisedGate` is the only kill path with tests (`suite-gate-supervisor.test.ts:175`, `orchestrator.test.ts:318`), and a second tree-kill seam for non-suite gates is a second thing to get wrong on Windows. The per-gate wall I object to in finding 2 is arguably a **feature** in the common case -- the observed v0.119.4 failure was one gate hanging, and a per-gate 20-minute wall catches it cleanly; the 49-gate cumulative case is hypothetical and has never been observed. And 48 extra worker spawns may be noise against a check run that already takes many minutes.

What would flip me: a measurement of `runSupervisedGate`'s fixed per-call cost -- worker spawn plus prune walk plus `Atomics.wait` setup -- against a realistic tee directory. Under roughly 50ms, 49x is under 2.5 seconds, finding 5 collapses to a footnote, and (a) becomes the better trade on single-mechanism grounds. Above a few hundred milliseconds it does not. That measurement does not exist on the thread, and the issue should not be bound without it, because it selects between (a) and (c).

## What I would need to change my verdict on the target

The recorded premise's conclusion -- a hung non-suite gate never 124s on the production cached path, and the fix is tree-kill plus an inherited deadline rather than a larger constant -- I could not break. I looked for four outs and all four closed: the cache does not replay a stale pass (`executor.ts:43`), advisory mode is off under full check mode (`check-mode.ts:94`), the soft-empty AC remap needs a literal `soft_empty` marker token a hung gate does not emit (`empty-resolution.ts:35`), and 124 does propagate through `finish` once produced.
